original_scope_and_findings: Original algorithm requested three generations only on M=M_E union M_O. The target theorem universally asserted a discrete lower bound whenever only M received three generations. The proof controlled cell residuals only on M and then incorrectly applied that bound to adjacent unmarked cells.

The native compatible two-triangle square refinement genuinely leaves an adjacent original triangle without an interior fine P1 node. This refutes availability of the written test, not the theorem inequality itself. No actual-data counterexample to the original universal inequality is claimed, and its proof remains unestablished for arbitrary marked-only refinement.

A polynomial cubic cell bubble or quadratic edge bubble is an ordinary H1-zero test, but not generally a fine P1 test; fine Galerkin orthogonality cannot justify substituting it in the discrete correction proof.

On a reference edge, the single midpoint nodal hat in the three-generation pattern has zero values at the quarter points and integral h_E/4, contradicting the former exact h_E/2 assertion. The new full-tent lift has quarter values one half and correctly has integral h_E/2. It is a different explicitly defined fine-space test.

Actual current-mesh nodal hats can shrink with arbitrary extra refinement. Both cell hats and edge lifts are therefore defined on the fixed original reference patterns and prolonged, preserving support, integrals and uniform scaling.

scope_preservation.preserved: All reliability and ordinary efficiency conclusions; discrete correction estimate with the same original edge-neighbor support; both contraction conclusions; optimal-complexity rate and approximation class; original deterministic bulk sets and bulk fractions; exact arithmetic and complete/budget-exhausted/invalid-input statuses; real constant-convection and symmetric model branches; existing choice assumptions.
scope_preservation.explicit_changed_interfaces: Algorithm refinement request is Q=P(M), with three generations on the entire original edge-neighbor patch. Target discrete estimate now explicitly assumes these patch patterns. This is an authorized coherent method repair and an explicit antecedent correction, not a claim that the original marked-only universal theorem was proved unchanged. The cumulative-count lemma retains generic request-set counting and adds the patch-expanded count in the original bulk marks.
scope_preservation.constants: At most four original triangles per bulk mark; at most seven virtual one-generation requests per patch triangle; cumulative C_cl=28C1/C2. C_eff may be chosen as the maximum of finite ordinary and discrete constants, depending only on shape and the stated convection scale. All displayed contraction parameter formulas and approximation rates remain valid with these actual method constants.

complete_local_proof: Uniform three-generation geometry has eight equal-area leaves and four incident to the interior median midpoint. Its reference P1 cell hat has integral |L|/6, L2 norm bounded by C h_L and gradient norm bounded by C. It vanishes on every original cell edge and belongs to the fine space by prolongation.

For each original L in omega(M), test the residual with its constant projected residual times this cell hat. The residual remainder is controlled by the original data oscillation; fine orthogonality changes the weak error form into the correction form. Scaling gives the cell lower bound on every incident neighbor, with the zero projected-residual case treated separately.

For each interior edge incident to M, prescribe its full triangular tent at all edge nodes of both fixed patterns and zero at every off-edge pattern node. The two piecewise-affine traces coincide even with different reference labels; other original edge traces vanish. The reference lift is continuous, supported in its two-cell patch, has edge integral h_E/2, L2 norm at most C h_E and gradient norm at most C.

Prolong that entire lift, not a new fine nodal hat, to the actual mesh. Testing the constant P1 jump times the lift leaves only that edge term. The cell lower bounds now apply on both incident triangles. Bounded overlap, at most four patches per triangle, proves the marked estimate on precisely omega(M).

The algorithm initializes flags on the original patch Q. Every requested descendant completes three generations; extra closure splits retain the flags appropriately. The finite recursive reinspection proof admits required grandchildren of coarser chain cells and gives the same generation/distance allocation mechanism.

Generic one-generation cumulative allocation bounds seven virtual requests per Q cell. Original edge-neighbor expansion gives |Q|<=4|M|, so all actual refinement and closure cells are bounded cumulatively by 28C1/C2 times the sum of original marks. No per-call cardinality or operation bound is asserted.

For contraction, M_E is a subset of M and its complete original neighbor patch is contained in Q; hence the repaired discrete lower bound applies. Oscillation and estimator reductions use only a subset of those refinements and can only improve under additional splits. For optimality, P0 data eliminate M_O and the comparison-cardinality argument still bounds the original M_E.
